name: XYZ Method buttock augmentation

card.summary: A surgical technique for placing silicone gluteal implants inside the gluteus maximus muscle using pelvic landmarks, aimed at rounder, fuller buttocks with more symmetrical, less visible implants.
card.aka: XYZ method, intramuscular gluteal augmentation (Gonzalez technique)
card.note: A surgical procedure with recognised complications such as wound opening, seroma and infection; performed by plastic surgeons.

quick.overview:
The XYZ method is an operation for gluteal implants developed by the Brazilian plastic surgeon Raul Gonzalez and published in 2004. It uses three points on the bony pelvis (X, Y and Z) and a line (G) to define a geometric plane for placing the implant inside the gluteus maximus muscle, rather than above or beneath it.

The appearance goal is rounder, projected, more symmetrical buttocks. The author's series of 746 patients operated between 1986 and 2003 reported good results, and a 2013 systematic review ranked the XYZ intramuscular pocket among the locations with the lowest complication rates.
quick.how: The procedure is performed by a plastic surgeon under anesthesia through an incision in the cleft between the buttocks. The surgeon uses the pelvic landmarks to guide dissection of a pocket in the muscle and places a silicone implant. Some series combine it with liposuction. Recovery guidance in general summaries of gluteal implant surgery mentions compression garments and several weeks of limited activity, with final contour appearing over months.
quick.risks: Reported complications of gluteal implants include wound dehiscence, seroma, infection, hematoma, asymmetry, capsular contracture and implant shifting. A 2013 review pooled rates of about 10 percent for wound dehiscence and about 2.5 percent for seroma across techniques. Nerve injury is described as a risk if dissection strays toward the sciatic area.

lead: The XYZ method is an intramuscular technique for gluteal implant surgery, described by Dr. Raul Gonzalez in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery in 2004 [1]. It addresses a known difficulty of buttock implants: dissecting inside the muscle without direct view can give uneven pockets and asymmetric results [1]. The method uses three points (X, Y and Z) and a line (G) on the pelvis to define the plane for dissection [1].

People seek gluteal augmentation to add volume, projection and a rounder contour to the buttocks. The XYZ approach places the implant within the gluteus maximus, a plane that proponents regard as reducing implant visibility and complications [2][3].

A 2018 review in Clinics in Plastic Surgery by the originating surgeon describes how the method uses the pelvic surface anatomy as a reference to help symmetry and lower implant visibility [3]. An independent 2013 systematic review compared pocket locations [2].

chain: Silicone implant placed inside the gluteus maximus using pelvic landmarks
Added volume and projection with symmetrical placement
angle.text: The implant adds volume to the buttocks, and the XYZ landmarks are intended to give a symmetrical, less visible result than freehand dissection. It is a surgical option people consider for a fuller gluteal shape.

paras: Gluteal implants have been placed in several planes, including submuscular, subfascial and intramuscular pockets. Intramuscular placement is considered by many surgeons to be superior, but dissecting within the muscle without reference points makes symmetry and safe depth hard to achieve [3].

The XYZ method addresses this with geometry. Points on the bony frame of the pelvis define the plane in which the muscle is detached, allowing a more precise and reproducible pocket [1][3]. General descriptions of gluteal implant surgery note that implants are placed through a midline incision and that surgeons take care to avoid structures such as the sacrum, the sacrotuberous ligament and the ischial tuberosity, since injury in that area can cause nerve problems [4].
The 2004 report described 746 patients operated on with the technique between 1986 and 2003 and concluded that it was safe and reproducible, with good results [1].

A 2013 systematic review of 30 articles covering five pocket locations reported pooled complication rates and ranked the intramuscular XYZ method lowest at 13.18 percent, ahead of submuscular (17.60 percent) and intramuscular (18.05 percent) placement; the most common complications overall were wound dehiscence (10.29 percent), seroma (2.49 percent), infection (1.12 percent) and hematoma (0.24 percent) [2].

A 2016 case series of 130 patients in an Asian ethnic group used the XYZ method with oval smooth silicone implants, with 90 percent also undergoing liposuction at the same time [5]. A broader 2019 meta-analysis summarised on Wikipedia found implants had a higher complication rate (31 percent) than fat grafting (7 percent) [4].

Implant-specific complications listed in general summaries include infection, wound dehiscence exposing the implant, rupture, seroma, capsular contracture, asymmetry, implant shifting, over-correction, sciatic nerve injury and paresthesia [4]. The same source gives full healing as about 6 to 8 months, with the final contour appearing at 6 months to a year, convalescence of four to six weeks, and advice to avoid strenuous exercise for three weeks and wear a compression garment [4].

timeline.event: Start of the series later reported by Gonzalez [1].
